small_guidance:
- The epilogue kernel is already memory-bound and tiny relative to the conv; further tuning of BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps will not move the needle. If keeping it, try BLOCK_SIZE=4096, num_warps=4, num_stages=2 and drop the divisions by precomputing `c_idx` via a 5D grid (pid_n, pid_c, pid_spatial) so channel index is free.
- Mask only the spatial tail: launch grid as (N*C, ceil(DHW/BLOCK)) so `c_idx = pid0 % C` is a cheap mod on a small constant; load scale/bias once per program (scalar) instead of per-element gather.
large_guidance:
- The conv3d dominates runtime (fast_p≈0.53 with epilogue already fused). Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with K = IC*kT*kH*kW reduced inside. Fuse the scaling_factor multiply, tanh, bias multiply, and sigmoid into the GEMM epilogue on the accumulator before storing — eliminates the separate epilogue kernel and an extra full read/write of the output tensor.
- Use channels-last-style indexing for the input gather (compute input offsets implicitly, no im2col materialization). Tile shape suggestion: BLOCK_M (OC) = 16 (matches out_channels=16, so a single tile covers all channels), BLOCK_N (spatial) = 64 or 128, BLOCK_K = 32; with kT*kH*kW=27 and IC=3, K=81 — one or two K-loop iterations only. Wrap in `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_N ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}.
- Precompute per-(kt,kh,kw) input offsets as constants outside the K-loop; bake kernel_size, stride=1, pad=0 as constexpr. Output shape is (128,16,14,62,62) ≈ 62M elements — bandwidth on store is the floor, so make sure the epilogue writes once and the K-reduction stays in registers.
